frozen_problem.title: An explicit Frobenius bound for triple products of elliptic curves
frozen_problem.statement: Is there a smooth projective $3$-fold $X$ over a finite field for which $H^3_{nr}(k(X)/k, \mathbb Q/\mathbb Z(2))$ is not zero?
frozen_problem.selection_basis: Rank 16, score 73.5; highest-ranked eligible outside cooldown and anti-thrashing gates, including the rank-15 packet in open draft PR19. Ranked, not provisional.

theory.target: Audit whether the imported B_X is the prime-to-characteristic determinant of all twenty H3 Frobenius eigenvalues, and isolate the unverified transfer from that determinant to unramified cohomology.
definitions: P_i(z)=z^2-t_i*z+q, roots counted with multiplicity; N_i=q+1-t_i.
R is the product of q^2 minus all eight triple roots; B=R*product_i N_i^2.
F20 is the rank-eight tensor plus two q*M_i blocks for each i; D20=det(q^2 I20-F20).
v_ell is the prime-adic valuation of a nonzero integer; ell must not divide q for the determinant comparison.
assumptions: Exact integer arithmetic; enumerate every nonsingular short Weierstrass model y^2=x^3+a*x+b over each listed prime field.
R=product over eight triple Frobenius roots of (q^2-root product); B=R*product_i(q+1-t_i)^2.
The twenty-dimensional model is (M1 tensor M2 tensor M3) direct sum two copies of q*Mi for each i.
Geometric identification uses standard elliptic-curve cohomology and Kunneth; no cycle-class computation or unramified group is computed.
All conclusions about l-adic determinants exclude l=p. No current parent-problem status is asserted.
approaches_considered: Quadratic-character point counts and exact Newton power sums.
Direct point enumeration and fraction-free determinant certificates.
Block determinant factorization and separate audit of the lattice-to-geometric transfer.
falsification_targets: Wrong q-power normalization or repeated-root multiplicity.
Infer integral saturation from rational invertibility.
Promote a lattice determinant to an unramified-cohomology bound without a comparison.

claims.statement: Two algorithms agree on 172 nonsingular curve models and 906 unordered trace triples over F5,F7,F11, including all R, B, D20 values.
claims.falsification_condition: A point-count, tuple-completeness, characteristic-polynomial or determinant mismatch.

claims.statement: For y^2=x^3+1 over F5 and its triple product, omitting six (2,1,0) summands gives v2(R)=4 instead of v2(D20)=10. The imported B already includes these summands.
claims.falsification_condition: An incorrect point count, decomposition, determinant or valuation.

claims.statement: The ordinary block calculation gives det(q^2 I20-F20)=q^18 B for all integer parameters. Its geometric interpretation and general lattice argument are not independently authored or kernel verified here.
claims.falsification_condition: A failed block factor q^3(q+1-t), multiplicity count, invertibility or lattice hypothesis.

claims.statement: The three tested zero-trace rows give B=q^12(q+1)^10, including B=14762250000000000 at q=5. This confirms arithmetic, not the imported vanishing assertion.
claims.falsification_condition: A mismatch in any tested exact determinant or closed-form row.

claims.statement: The imported claim that #H3_nr divides ell^v_ell(B) is unverified here. The available summary does not supply the integral cycle-class/divisible-part control or a justified subquotient comparison.
claims.falsification_condition: An actual geometric group exceeding the claimed bound would falsify it; a missing proof alone does not.

claims.statement: Colliot-Thelene and Kahn arXiv:1104.3350v3 Theorem 2.2 locates the relevant cycle-class obstruction; its object and hypotheses differ from a bare H3 determinant calculation.
claims.falsification_condition: A wrong theorem locator, object, hypothesis or reading.

progress.summary: Exact F5 trace-zero witness rejects the omitted-summand shortcut: v2 changes from 4 to 10.
Frobenius arithmetic reconstructed on 906 trace triples and three zero-trace closed forms.
Separate the checked determinant from the missing comparison to the geometric group in the available evidence.
